rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only performance. This tests the importance of RNA data alone and isolates the impact of the RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and profile setting (singleprofile). It clarifies whether RNA modality is sufficient, which is critical for understanding modality-specific contributions before exploring multimodal combinations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile (config_002) improves performance while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation consistent. It isolates the impact of profile setting, a key design choice, and addresses uncertainty about whether multi-profile data enhances accuracy. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly compares a critical design decision with minimal variable changes.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) in the multiprofile setup improves performance, isolating the impact of representation choice. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile advantage with exploration of encoder improvements, avoiding unnecessary changes to aggregation or fusion methods.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005, 0.65 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and PCA-based models. This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 (best RNA encoder) with resnet50 (strong image encoder) in a multimodal multiprofile setup using avgpool (proven effective in config_005) and concat fusion. It isolates the impact of multimodal integration while building on established effective components, balancing exploration of modality fusion with exploitation of prior successes.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other settings the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly addresses whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, providing critical insight into the importance of this design choice without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with multiprofile and transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.653) outperform others. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a new representation) while keeping multiprofile and transformer aggregation (same as config_006) isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It directly compares scgpt vs scvi_n200 under identical aggregation settings, addressing a key design decision with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (rna_only with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation) achieves the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether adding a strong image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with the same RNA encoder and transformer aggregation can improve performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation (building on the best RNA-only setup) and exploration (testing multimodal potential), while avoiding redundant changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the impact of aggregation/fusion choices. It clarifies whether the transformer aggregation and weighted fusion in config_039 are critical for performance, balancing exploitation of strong evidence with exploration of design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether using avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (instead of transformer aggregation) maintains high performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It directly compares two key design choices (aggregation type) while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion type constant, providing critical insight under limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_039) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods the same) affects performance. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the strong evidence from config_039.
